body.statement:
There exists \(\varepsilon_0=\varepsilon_0(d,m,\alpha, eta,s,L)>0\) such that, for every \(0<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}\le\varepsilon_0\), the functions \(g_{\mathrm{sep}}(x)=\cos(2\pi x_1)\), \(h_{\mathrm{sep}}(y)=\cos(2\pi y_1)\), and \(\eta_{\pm}(y\mid x)=1\pm\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}g_{\mathrm{sep}}(x)h_{\mathrm{sep}}(y)\) are normalized positive smooth conditional densities. With \(e\equiv1/2\) and the uniform arm-\(0\) witness, they induce two laws in \(\mathcal M_{0,\mathrm{unif}}(d,m,\alpha, eta,s,L)\). Because \(\int_{\mathcal X}g_{\mathrm{sep}}(x)\,dx=0\), \(Q_+=Q_-=\operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal Y)\) and \(W_1(Q_+,Q_-)=0\), whereas \(W_1\{\eta_+(y\mid x)\,dy,\eta_-(y\mid x)\,dy\}=2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}|g_{\mathrm{sep}}(x)|/\pi^2\) and \(\int_{\mathcal X}W_1\{\eta_+(y\mid x)\,dy,\eta_-(y\mid x)\,dy\}\,dx=4\varepsilon_{\mathrm{sep}}/\pi^3>0\). More generally, for any measurable probability kernels \(\mu_x\) and \(
u_x\), \[W_1\!\left(\int_{\mathcal X}\mu_x\,dx,\int_{\mathcal X}
u_x\,dxight)\le\int_{\mathcal X}W_1(\mu_x,
u_x)\,dx.\] Consequently, GANICE's extended-loss lower bound and its continuous-conditioning minimax upper/lower theory, which is matched only up to logarithmic and implementation-transfer factors, do not transfer as a marginal-mixture \(W_1\) frontier. Compatible extended-loss upper bounds can nevertheless imply generally nonsharp marginal upper bounds through this convexity inequality.
body.justification: The smooth equal-marginal separation prevents design-averaged conditional transport theory from being mistaken for the weaker marginal-mixture transport problem while recording the valid one-way upper-bound implication.
body.gap: TamanoImaizumi2026GANICE Definition 1 and equations (1)--(2) define extended Wasserstein loss as design-averaged statewise \(W_1\); Theorem 2 gives a logarithmically inflated upper bound under an implementation-transfer condition, and Theorem 3 gives the continuous-conditioning lower bound. The proposition shows that its loss can stay positive when the present marginal \(W_1\) is exactly zero.
body.consumer: A referee or practitioner comparing GANICE with the known-design marginal reconstruction benchmark can distinguish its nontransferable extended-loss lower bound and continuous-conditioning upper/lower theory from the valid, generally nonsharp convexity-based marginal upper implication.
